title: Employee Information Management Policy
content: This policy establishes the specific requirements, decision rules, responsibilities, and controls for employee information management. It is intended to give employees and managers a clear process for making compliant decisions and documenting exceptions.

title: Employee Information Management Policy
content: This policy applies to employee information management activities performed by employees and managers. Other workers are covered when their engagement terms, role assignment, or approved business arrangement places them under the policy. Eligibility depends on the role, activity, location, and conditions stated in the policy rules below.

title: Employee Information Management Policy
content:
- Employees must update legal name, contact information, emergency contacts, and bank details through the HR Service Portal within 10 business days of a change.
- Changes to legal identity or work authorization require supporting documentation before HR updates the personnel record.
- Managers may view only employee information required for legitimate supervisory duties and must not export personnel records to personal devices.

title: Employee Information Management Policy
content: Employees submit changes through the HR Service Portal. HR Operations validates supporting documents, updates the master record, and records the completion date. Managers are notified only when the change affects payroll, scheduling, access, or another business process.

title: Employee Information Management Policy
content: Urgent corrections affecting payroll or work authorization are escalated to HR Operations on the same business day. If required evidence is unavailable, HR may place the change on hold rather than overwrite the existing record.

title: Employee Information Management Policy
content: Employees are responsible for providing accurate information, following the approved workflow, retaining required evidence, and raising questions before taking action when the requirement is unclear. Managers are responsible for reviewing requests consistently, confirming business need, and escalating cases that fall outside their authority. The policy owner is responsible for maintaining the rule, communicating material changes, and reviewing the policy at least annually.

title: Employee Information Management Policy
content: Approvals, supporting documents, decisions, and exception records must be retained in the approved company system according to the applicable retention schedule. The policy owner reviews this policy at least annually and sooner when legal, business, security, or operational requirements change.

title: Employee Information Management Policy
content: An employee changes their legal name after marriage. They upload the required legal document through the HR Service Portal. HR validates it, updates the personnel record, and confirms the change before the next payroll cutoff.

title: Employee Information Management Policy
content:
- How do I update my employee information?
- Where do I change my emergency contact?
- What documents are required for a legal name change?
- Can my manager change my personnel record?
- How quickly must I report a change in my personal information?
- Who can access my employee records?
- What happens if a payroll-related record is incorrect?

title: Annual Leave Policy
content:
- Employees receive annual leave according to their employment terms and must request planned leave through the Leave Portal before the absence begins.
- Planned leave of 1–3 working days should normally be submitted at least 3 working days in advance; leave of 4 or more working days should normally be submitted at least 10 working days in advance.
- Managers must consider team coverage, operational deadlines, and overlapping leave before approving a request.

title: Annual Leave Policy
content: The employee submits dates and leave type in the Leave Portal. The direct manager reviews coverage and either approves, rejects, or requests a revised date. HR records approved leave and the portal becomes the authoritative attendance record.

title: Annual Leave Policy
content: Emergency leave may be reported after the absence begins when the employee cannot reasonably submit a request in advance. The employee must notify the manager as soon as practical and submit the request retrospectively.

title: Data Accuracy Policy
content:

- Employees who identify an inaccurate record must report it through the Data Quality Portal within 2 business days when the error could affect a customer, employee, legal, or financial decision.
- No employee may silently overwrite disputed data; corrections must preserve the original value and record who made the change, when, and why.

title: Data Accuracy Policy
content: The requester submits the affected record, evidence of the correct value, and the business impact through the Data Quality Portal. The data owner validates the evidence, approves the correction, and records the change in the audit trail.

content: If an immediate correction is necessary to prevent material harm, the data owner may authorize a temporary correction and must complete the formal audit record within 1 business day.
